candidates.decision_relevance: A complete settled ETF breadth/flow sequence would test whether proxy breadth and price deterioration were confirmed or contradicted by the intended completed-week institutional-flow evidence.
candidates.evidence_reference: W35-W37 weekly adversarial reviews; daily outputs on 2026-09-15 through 2026-09-17
candidates.metric_name: Settled BTC/ETH ETF daily net-flow and breadth sequence
candidates.missing_history_problem: Only isolated settled sessions or an unavailable completed-week sequence are reported. Within-week persistence, concentration, and sequencing relative to price, breadth, and liquidity cannot be assessed.

candidates.decision_relevance: A fixed-universe, time-stamped breadth history would materially distinguish persistent participation deterioration from endpoint noise and would test whether ETH/BTC strength broadened beyond narrow leadership.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly describe top-100 or rich breadth as point-in-time proxy-only, with changing membership; weekly reviews cite unavailable settled ETF breadth.
candidates.metric_name: Fixed-universe cross-sectional breadth, participation, and leadership history
candidates.missing_history_problem: Available observations are snapshots with changing membership and no intrawweek path, so breadth lead-lag, persistence, broadening, and leadership concentration cannot be audited.

candidates.decision_relevance: Complete, time-stamped liquidation and leverage-flow events would establish whether stress preceded weakness, represented a transient reset, or persisted through the drawdown.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs from 2026-09-14 through 2026-09-17; W35-W37 reviews
candidates.metric_name: Complete liquidation composition and open-interest change event history
candidates.missing_history_problem: Liquidation totals are lower bounds from a fragile, completeness-unverified source, while long/short composition, venue coverage, and temporal order are unavailable.

candidates.decision_relevance: Point-in-time hourly histories of price, ETH/BTC, funding, open interest, taker flow, and depth would resolve whether adverse microstructure and leverage observations led or followed price weakness and whether rebounds persisted.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly cite unavailable 1-hour horizons, shortened nominal windows, mixed timestamps, and conflicting 4h/12h/24h/72h paths.
candidates.metric_name: Cutoff-clean hourly price, relative-performance, leverage, and microstructure sequence
candidates.missing_history_problem: Current records are snapshots or irregular horizons; actual spans and observation order are inconsistent or unavailable, preventing lead-lag and sequence-error testing.

candidates.decision_relevance: Frozen candidate objects and point-in-time feature snapshots would allow direct audit of hindsight leakage, target precision, horizon alignment, and whether completed-week information entered the warning narrative.
candidates.evidence_reference: All W33-W37 weekly reviews report three prior candidates but omit their objects; daily outputs contain only contemporaneous candidate examples.
candidates.metric_name: Frozen candidate registry with issue times, cutoffs, feature snapshots, and specifications
candidates.missing_history_problem: Candidate counts are reported without the underlying issue timestamps, metric paths, bounds, thresholds, rationales, and available-information snapshots, making ex-ante audit and falsifiability checks impossible.

candidates.decision_relevance: Matured candidate and exit-warning outcomes would quantify false positives, false negatives, post-warning upside, drawdown protection, and range containment rather than leaving timing risk unscored.
candidates.evidence_reference: W33-W37 reviews and all daily outputs state matured outcome or action-compass rows are absent or null.
candidates.metric_name: Matured forecast and exit-warning outcome history
candidates.missing_history_problem: No matured rows or scored outcomes are supplied, so the opportunity cost of premature warnings and the protection from delayed recognition cannot be estimated.

candidates.decision_relevance: A cutoff-aligned macro history would provide independent context for distinguishing crypto-specific breadth/liquidity deterioration from broader risk-asset or dollar-driven moves.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs on 2026-09-14 through 2026-09-17 repeatedly report missing, stale, or unavailable macro context.
candidates.metric_name: Cutoff-aligned dollar, volatility, rates, and broad risk-asset macro sequence
candidates.missing_history_problem: Macro observations are absent or stale and cannot be sequenced against crypto price, breadth, ETF flows, or leverage changes.
